subject: Possible identification issue concerning the interaction between grouping variables

messages.author: 9044165ad6889125
messages.subject: Possible identification issue concerning the interaction between grouping variables
parts:
Hi folks,

There is a model I'm testing that involves a two-way interaction effect on a latent variable. Essentially, there are two grouping variables that reflect experimental conditions (a and b; which below correspond to Acc and Type), each of which corresponds to two conditions (let's say a1 and a2, b1 and b2). Now, my model does not pose direct effects of the conditions on my latent factor of interest (which below is 'POFA'). Rather, it poses that a difference will emerge (say between a1 and a2) only in one condition (let's say b1). In other words, there is only an interaction effect (denoted below via INTAccType). 

Now, to test this, we've ONLY included the interaction term in our model.

DissSEM3 <- '
  # latent variable definitions - Bifactor added
    POFA   =~ PercepAcc1 + PercepAcc2 + PercepAcc3 + PercepAcc4Reco + PercepAcc5
  #Structure
  POFA ~ FdbkValN + INTAccType
'

Here is the rub: we also had a third grouping factor pertaining to a third set of experimental conditions (let's say, c1 and c2) where we posed a direct effect of this condition on the latent factor (in the code above, this is the effect of FdbkValN –> POFA). The results suggested that we created a suppression effect by accident in that this third factor is negatively associated with the outcome (it should be positively correlated). You see, this third pair of conditions (c1 and c2) is correlated with one of the condition factors that comprise our interaction term (and these conditions are not included in our model above). This dependency in the data was expected but we are not sure how to account for what seems to be a model misspecification issue. When we include the condition factor, we consistently encountered issues related to identification or a solution not being found.

Ideally, the model would like like this:
DissSEM3 <- '
  # latent variable definitions - Bifactor added
    POFA   =~ PercepAcc1 + PercepAcc2 + PercepAcc3 + PercepAcc4Reco + PercepAcc5
  #Structure
  POFA ~ FdbkValN + Acc + INTAccType
'
 
Unfortunately, this model generates this data:
Error in fit.indep@test[[2]] : subscript out of bounds

Please advise and thanks in advance!

Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Possible identification issue concerning the interaction between grouping variables
parts:
there is only an interaction effect (denoted below via INTAccType). 

Now, to test this, we've ONLY included the interaction term in our model.

Without the lower-order terms for Acc and Type, the effect of the dummy code "INTAccType" is not interpretable as an interaction term.  Instead it merely distinguishes the group in which both Acc == 1 and Type == 1 from the group containing all other cases (both == 0 or only one or the other variable == 1).  Not sure how this will affect your unexpected anomaly.
Ideally, the model would like like this:

#Structure
  POFA ~ FdbkValN + Acc + INTAccType

No like this:

POFA ~ FdbkValN + Acc + Type + INTAccType

Not to mention including the 3-way interaction (and all 2-way interactions) with the third factor, for which you only include a lower-order effect.  Also not sure how that would affect your results.
Error in fit.indep@test[[2]] : subscript out of bounds

This seems strange. Are you using the latest lavaan (0.6-6)?  Including a reproducible script (and data?) could help track down the issue.

Hi folks,

Turns out that the "subscript out of bounds error" is due to my having an outdated version of lavaan. Updating to .6-6 fixed this issue. 

Terrence – I see what you are pointing out regarding the interaction terms. We did mean-center the variables so that the interaction term reflects all condition levels (at least I think it does in that we have 4 distinct values for this variable). Still, I re-ran the model you specified and things worked out...

...now, here is my issue. In theory, the interaction we specified is what we might call a pure interaction (i.e., only the combination of x and w – xw – should impact y). The model you specified suggests that there are also effects of x and w. I suppose that these become a topic of diiscussion as a matter of principle, but if you would comment on this point I'd (i.e., adding these terms improves fit but is atheoretical) I'd greatly appreciate it. 

Thanks for your help! I greatly appreciate your time.

Chris

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Possible identification issue concerning the interaction between grouping variables
parts: We did mean-center the variables

The predictors?  I don't think it makes sense to mean-center dummy codes.  I think this would make them weighted effects-codes (see Cohen, Cohen, West, & Aiken, 2003, section 8.4 --- chapter 9 about interactions with categorical predictors should also be illuminating).
...now, here is my issue. In theory, the interaction we specified is what we might call a pure interaction (i.e., only the combination of x and w – xw – should impact y).

If x and w are dummy codes and only the combination of x==1 and w==1 produces a change in the mean, then that is consistent with a model in which the slopes of lower-order terms (x and w) are both zero.  That is, you test that null hypothesis by testing whether fixing the simple slopes of x and w to zero significantly diminishes model fit.  

You don't test the null hypothesis of no interaction by fitting a model without lower-order terms, but rather by testing the x:w slope for significance while allowing x and w to have nonzero simple slopes (which might also be zero in the population).  Testing the x:w slope in a model without simple effects of x and w is positing a 2-group model (x and w == 1 vs. x and/or w != 1), as opposed to the 4-group model that allows you to test the interaction between 2 binary factors.  You can do it, but I would not call it interaction, because you don't have 2 variables interacting in your model; you would just have a multiplicative composite dummy variable.  Just my 2 cents.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
